query: how to build a customer requests desk from your inbox
title: Build a customer requests desk from your inbox | 50agents
description: Turn your inbox into a requests desk: one record per request with status, priority and an answer-by date, a board by status, and replies drafted.
h1: How to build a customer requests desk from your inbox
answer: Give every customer email that needs an answer its own record with a status (New, Waiting on us, Waiting on them, Solved), a priority and an answer-by date, and work from a board of those records instead of the inbox.
You can do it with Gmail labels for a few a day, a shared inbox for a small team, or a desk app that pulls requests from email and drafts the replies.

body.p: SupportBee, which sells both, puts the line at about 10 support staff or 200 requests a day: below it a shared inbox works, above it a help desk pays off. Its signs it is time to move: two people answering the same email, messages missed, and more time spent coordinating than answering.

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: Pick one address for requests
steps.body: support@ or help@. Requests to personal inboxes get lost when someone is away.

steps.title: Decide what becomes a request
steps.body: A question, a problem, a change, a complaint. Not newsletters, invoices or sales pitches.

steps.title: Create a record per request
steps.body: By hand from a label, or automatically from new email. Keep the thread link on the record.

steps.title: Sort each one
steps.body: Kind, priority and answer-by date as it arrives. Rules first, then judgement for the unclear ones.

steps.title: Work from the board
steps.body: Waiting on us, oldest first, urgent at the top. The inbox becomes where replies go out, not where work is tracked.

steps.title: Close the loop
steps.body: Waiting on them for three days with no reply: a short check-in, then Solved.

body: Captain builds this desk from one sentence. It asks where requests come in and whether replies should go out from your email, then builds the requests list, a Desk board by status, an Urgent view and the Overview numbers. Its AI agent, Desk, sorts each new request (kind, priority, answer-by date, a line on why) and drafts a reply to each question from what your business knows; if it is not sure of an answer it says what it would need instead of guessing. Every reply waits for your yes.

wrong.title: Two people answer the same email
wrong.body: Nobody could see who had it. Assign each request to one person, or have one person own the desk.

wrong.title: A thread splits
wrong.body: The customer replies with a new subject and it becomes a new request. Match on the customer’s email and merge.

wrong.title: Everything is urgent
wrong.body: Priority by gut feel drifts up. Write the rule for Urgent in one sentence and stick to it.

wrong.title: Forwarded requests lose the customer
wrong.body: A colleague forwards an email and the request shows the colleague as the customer. Read the original sender from the forwarded text.

wrong.title: Drafts that promise too much
wrong.body: An AI-drafted reply offers a refund you would not give. Keep policies in its memory, and review every draft before it goes.

faqs.a: A shared inbox for a small team with modest volume; a help desk once you have many support staff, several channels or service-level targets to report on.

faqs.q: How do I stop two people replying to the same email?
faqs.a: Assign each conversation to one person. Google Groups’ Collaborative Inbox lets members take a conversation; a desk app shows each request’s owner and status.

faqs.q: How do I track open customer requests?
faqs.a: Give each one a record with a status and an answer-by date, and work from a view of everything Waiting on us, oldest first.
